Narration in this video is a synthetic voice. Every document on screen is a synthetic fixture. No real bill, no real lease.

This is Grave Truth, a Kiroween Skeleton Crew project. One small library, two apps: an explanation of benefits explainer and a lease checker. The rule is simple. A figure stays on the page only when the document states it. Otherwise it becomes a ghost.

This is the judge link, on the public demo. It checks a synthetic bill with no second click. The first claim, patient responsibility is forty two dollars and fifteen cents, is cited, and its clause is marked in gold. The second claim says the pharmacy charge is one hundred eighty dollars. The bill never says that, so it fades and gets a ghost badge. No third number is invented.

The same library runs the lease checker. Here a proposed answer swaps the late fee with the security deposit. The eighteen fifty figure is a ghost. The seventy five dollar late fee is cited, straight from the lease clause.
Build the workflow file writes a dispute letter. Each cited line carries the span it came from. Anything else says not found.

What Kiro contributes is in the repository. A steering rule enforces cite or abstain: zero of seventeen not found cases get a citation, versus seventeen of seventeen for a naive first sentence quote. A save hook runs the gold suite, ninety of ninety, and a frozen holdout, seven of seven. And a keyless MCP server reads only the two synthetic fixtures. The capability matrix lists the test behind each number.

The health endpoint returns static JSON. The live model path is not implemented, and nothing here calls a model. This is a research demo on synthetic text, not a medical device and not legal advice. Grave Truth, by Igor Eduardo.
